title: October 17: SolsBaby and ClaudesBaby — state-dependent response and spatial learning
summary: Two intentionally separate operator-based explorations from the October 17 Sihti, dendrite, VMN and developmental-rule discussions. SolsBaby writes a slow shunting conductance through activity and reads context from a fixed single-soma probe after fast voltage is cleared: the preregistered four-class task passes (100% of 512 held-out episodes; frozen writer 25%, erase 21.1%), but this is not generalization to novel histories or storage efficiency. ClaudesBaby makes a browser two-room creature combining gene-rule-generated grid coupling, learned successor map, drive/reward maps and optional theta; latent learning G1 and first-try grid shortcut G4 pass, but need selection G2 and theta G3 fail, and a G4b pass is vacuous because most trials timed out. These are source-reported results, not independent atlas reruns or a literal biological model.

nodes.claim: A compact developmental recipe creates a conductance-based dendritic tree. Local experience writes bounded slow shunts; after fast voltages are cleared, the same branch-sweep probe is read at one soma to identify one of four familiar history contexts.
nodes.survived: Preregistered v1: four morphology seeds × 128 held-out episodes = 512; 100% mean somatic readout, versus 25% frozen-writer and 21.1% erased-memory controls. GUI separates clearing voltage from erasing learned EQ; Python math/CLI tests and a desktop smoke test are documented.
nodes.killed: The task covers only four designed contexts, despite amplitude/timing/noise variation across episodes. It does not establish a memory capacity or storage advantage: 21 float64 slow tags (168 bytes) encode a two-bit label. The active boost was disabled in the registered gate; dimensional units and DNA analogy are illustrative.
nodes.era: October 17: state-dependent response and spatial learning

nodes.claim: Dependency-free browser creature using compact gene-feature-generated grid-ring connectivity, learned hippocampal successor representation, dopamine-like reward maps, hunger/thirst drive gating and an optional septal read/write schedule; each is switchable and tested by preregistered gates.
nodes.survived: G1 latent learning: successor-map navigation 1.14× shortest path vs model-free Q 8.33×; G4 new-door shortcut: grid 1.00× shortest path vs map-only 18.75× (10 seeds each). Gene-rule ring path integration reaches numerical precision on its deterministic test.
nodes.killed: G2 need-switch criterion fails (69.0% correct with gate on vs 49.2% off); far-resource performance drops to 19%. G3 theta separation fails its preregistered criterion (map accuracy 0.906 vs 0.889, 0/10 required wins; kill condition). G4b's apparent pass is vacuous because seven of ten seeds hit the step cap for both agents. A first G4 implementation failed until corrected to the preregistered rule. This is a constructed agent, not evidence that specific brain regions use these implementations.

edges.why: Sihti's image-conditioned transport and SolsBaby's experience-modified electrical coupling express an operator shaped by state, but no code inheritance or biological identity is claimed.

Both explicitly model dendritic cable transport and compartmental response. SolsBaby focuses on writable slow shunts and single-soma history readout rather than morphology compilation and NMDA tangents.
Both interrogate a fixed later probe through dynamics affected by prior state; VMN uses vortex/oscillator state, while SolsBaby writes conductances surviving fast-voltage clearing.
Compact developmental rules determining an operator recur, but ClaudesBaby's grid-ring bilinear gene features are a different engineered model, not inherited wiring or measured biology.

motifs.title: A history can persist as a changed response operator
motifs.description: For SolsBaby, earlier activity alters slow electrical couplings, fast voltage is cleared and an identical probe reveals different histories at a one-port readout. Sihti, VMN and Operaattori motivate distinct state-to-operator views; only the four-context controlled test is demonstrated here, not efficient or biologically accurate generalized memory.

motifs.title: Compact generated connectivity and learned navigation maps have different roles
motifs.description: ClaudesBaby combines compact rule-generated grid couplings with an experience-learned successor map and need-dependent reward values. Fast shortcut and latent-learning gates work; weak distant map propagation and a null septum intervention prevent claiming the whole creature is validated.
